Dr Jack Thomas
Department of Gastroenterology
City Hospital
Main Road
Stillwater

21/02/2015

Dear Dr Thomas

Re: Mr Patrick Newton

DOB: 6/07/1989

Thank you for seeing Mr Newton, a 25 year old accountant, whose clinical features are consistent with
possible inflammatory bowel disease.

Commented [jc1]: 25-year-old

Mr Newton is single and lives with his parents. However, he is a heavy smoker, he is a regular squash
player. It is worth mentioning that his uncle has Crohn's disease.

Commented [jc2]: ?

Initially, he presented to my practice complaining of chronic mild diarrhoea and lower quadrant abdominal
pain which began four month ago. This was associated with lethargy and loss of appetite. Interestingly, he
lost three kilograms in the past four months. Of note, his condition affected his daily activity.
Unfortunately, diet modification was not successful in alleviating the symptoms.

On examination, there was no hepato-splenomegaly but there was generalized abdominal tenderness.
Apart from the aforementioned findings, the rest of his examination was normal. No abnormalities could
be detected in his investigations apart from mild anaemia, elevated white cell count, elevated CRP and
positive occult blood in stool.

In view of the above, my provisional diagnosis is Crohn's disease versus ulcerative colitis. It would be
appreciated if you could take over his ongoing care. Should there be any quires, please do not hesitate to
contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
